transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate your time. Um... I guess I'm here because my family wanted me to come, and I always try to do what they think is best. They... well, they seem to think I'm just imagining things, which is silly, really. I mean, I don't want to sound like a bother or anything, but... I know for a fact that the hospital people, and even some folks from the cleaning agency I work for, they've been... well, they've been keeping an eye on my house. And my cleaning routes, too. Just to make sure I'm taking proper care of my husband. I mean, it's nice of them to care, right? But my family thinks I'm making it up. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been hearing voices that other people cannot hear?

Oh... um. Well, I don't want you to think poorly of me, Doctor. I know how it sounds, but it's really nothing bad. Sometimes... even when the house is completely quiet, I do hear... well, a woman's voice. 

She's usually right near the kitchen window. She just tells me to check the locks, or maybe to move my husband's pills. It's just so clear, exactly as if she is standing right there with me. I just figure it's my own mind trying to make sure I'm doing a good job taking care of things, since I'm so used to keeping everything in order for work and at home. That's pretty normal, isn't it? I really hope that doesn't make me sound... well, you know. I'm just trying my best.
How long have these experiences been happening?

Um... well, let's see. I'd say... maybe around 11 months? Yes, about 11 months since I first started noticing the woman's voice and... and feeling like the hospital and cleaning folks were keeping an eye on us. 

I know that probably sounds like a long time, but it really hasn't been a bother, I promise. It's just been a quiet little thing in the background while I go about my days. I haven't let it get in the way of my work or taking care of my husband, not at all. Eleven months isn't too unusual for something like this, is it? I hope I should have mentioned it sooner, but I just didn't want to make a fuss over nothing.
During this time, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed?

Oh, um... depressed? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, everyone has a down day here or there, right? Especially when you're busy with work and taking care of a house and a husband. But... no, not for two whole weeks, and certainly not *very* depressed. 

I always try to keep a smile on and just keep moving forward. It's so important to stay positive, don't you think? I wouldn't want anyone to think I wasn't grateful for everything I have. So, no, I don't think I've felt like that. I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I'm just trying to be honest with you.
Have you noticed any times when your thoughts or speech felt jumbled or hard for other people to follow?

Oh... well, I suppose... sometimes. I really try to be clear, I promise I do. But every now and then, when I try to explain what is happening, my mind is just moving so fast because of everything I have to do. 

The words sort of run together. Like, I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then somehow it runs right into the church schedule, and then the numbers on my client list for work... and people will say they just can't follow me. I don't mean to confuse anyone, I really don't. I just have so much to keep track of, and it all just spills out at once. That happens to everyone when they have a lot on their plate, doesn't it? I hope it doesn't make me sound foolish... I'm really trying my best to communicate properly with everyone.
Have you ever had times when the voices or feeling watched were only present when your mood was very high or very low?

Oh... um, let me think. I wouldn't say they only happen when my mood is... well, up or down. Actually, there was a... a quieter spell, just for several weeks. I was sleeping a bit more, taking it easy, and not rushing around quite as much as I usually do with my cleaning work and all. 

But... well, I still heard the voice by the kitchen window during that time. And I still believed the agency was watching us, even when I was just resting and feeling perfectly fine. I hope it's alright that I'm telling you this... I don't want you to think I'm completely out of sorts. It's just that those things stayed around even when everything else in my mind was quiet. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Have these experiences lasted continuously for at least six months?

Oh, um... well, it's been a while now. I hope it's okay to say it's been going on for a bit. It started... oh, let's see, about a year and two months ago? Yes, right around the time my husband was in the hospital for his heart. 

That was such a stressful time, as you can imagine. I think anyone would be a little out of sorts after something like that, wouldn't they? I really tried to hold everything together for him, but... well, yes, it's been about that long since all these changes started. I hope that's not too long... I've just been trying to manage it all as best as I can on my own. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or motivation in things you usually enjoy?

Oh... um, no, I don't think so. I really try to keep my spirits up and stay busy. I still enjoy making a nice dinner for my husband, and... well, keeping the house tidy, my evening programs, things like that. 

I wouldn't want to just sit around and let things go, I promise I always try to stay on top of my chores and be helpful. I hope that's a good sign? I really do try my best to keep a positive attitude and keep doing all the things I'm supposed to do. Is it okay that I haven't lost interest in those things?
Have these experiences caused you to have trouble keeping up with work, home responsibilities, or relationships?

Oh... um... I really hate to admit this part. I've always prided myself on being a good, dependable worker, you know? But... well, at my job with the cleaning agency, they... they actually had to take away my supervisory routes recently. I guess some of the clients and my coworkers mentioned that they couldn't rely on my work quite the way they used to. I feel just awful about it, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm lazy or a bad employee—I've just been so overwhelmed by everything going on, and I guess it showed more than I realized. 

And at home... well, my husband and our pastor, they've had to step in a little more lately. Just to help out with things. They felt I wasn't keeping up with the caregiving and the household responsibilities very safely. It's so embarrassing to say out loud to you... a wife should be able to take care of her own home, shouldn't she? 

I promise I'm trying my very best to get back on track and do better. I really am. I hope you're not too disappointed in me for letting things slip like this... is it normal to struggle with these things when you're going through a tough patch?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least one week when you felt unusually energized or irritable?

Oh... well, um... I really try to keep a sweet temper, I promise I do. But... yes, I suppose there are stretches, sometimes for a week or more, where I actually feel just wonderfully bright and strong. Like I have all the energy in the world and I can just handle absolutely everything, you know? I hope it's okay to feel that way sometimes, it's actually quite nice to have that extra energy to get things done! 

But... well, I really hate to admit this part, because I'm usually such a peaceful person... during those times, if my husband or one of my cleaning clients questions me about how I'm doing something, I... I can get a little short. Actually, I end up snapping at them much harder than I ever mean to. I feel just awful about it afterward, I really do, and I always try to apologize. I hope you don't think I'm a mean or angry person for losing my patience like that... does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed a reduced ability to feel or show emotion, or a lack of motivation to do things?

Oh... um, no, I don't think so. I really do try to keep a smile on my face and stay warm with people. I'd hate for anyone to think I was being cold or unfeeling, you know? I always make sure to ask my clients how their day is going and I try to be cheerful for my husband when he gets home. 

And as for motivation... well, like I mentioned before, I really do try my best to keep busy and stay on top of my chores and my evening programs. I want to be helpful and do what's expected of me. I hope I'm doing a good job of explaining that... I just really wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just gives up and stops caring about things. Is it a good sign that I still try to keep my spirits up and stay active?
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other recreational drugs around the time these experiences started?

Oh, goodness, no. No, absolutely not. I really hope you don't think I would do anything like that. I've always been very careful to live a good, clean life, you know? I don't drink—maybe just a tiny sip of champagne at a wedding, but that's all—and I would never, ever touch any kind of drugs. 

I know some people struggle with those things, and I'm not judging them, but... well, I just wouldn't want to do anything that could upset my husband or our pastor, or make me look bad at work. I try so hard to be a respectable person. You believe me, don't you? I promise I'm telling the truth about that.
Have you ever done anything that seemed very odd or hard for others to understand because of these beliefs or the voice?

Oh... well... um... I really hope this doesn't sound too strange. I don't want you to think I'm doing anything bad or... or crazy. It's just... well, sometimes, both at my clients' houses and at home, I... I catch myself doing this little routine. 

I'll start lining up the cleaning bottles, and the towels, and... and even the chairs. I have to put them in these very specific patterns. And then I'll walk back through the rooms, just over and over again, checking on them. It just... it feels so wrong to leave them any other way, like something terrible might happen if they aren't just so. 

I know it probably looks a little odd if someone catches me doing it, but I promise it's just my way of making sure everything is perfectly neat and tidy. Being thorough is a good quality for a housekeeper to have, right? I just... I hope you don't think less of me for being a little particular about things.
Have you ever had a period of at least four days when you felt much more energetic or irritable than usual and needed much less sleep?

Oh... well, I suppose there are times like that, yes. I always try to use that extra energy to be helpful, though! There are stretches where I just feel so... bright and strong. Like I can handle absolutely everything, all the heavy cleaning and the errands, and I really don't feel like I need much rest at all to do it. It's actually quite nice to get so much done for people. 

But... oh, I do feel terrible admitting this part... sometimes during those stretches, if my husband or one of my clients questions me about something, I... well, I snap at them. Much harder than I mean to. 

I always feel just awful about it afterward, because I'd never want to be rude or disrespectful. I always try to apologize and make it up to them right away. I hope you don't think I'm a mean person... I really do try my best to be sweet and patient. It's perfectly normal to get a little short-tempered when you're working so hard, isn't it?
During those times when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep, did you also believe you had special powers, a special mission, or other unusually grand abilities?

Oh, my... "special powers" sounds so... so boastful, doesn't it? I would never want to sound arrogant. I really don't think I'm better than anyone else, I promise you that. 

It's just... well... during those times when I have all that extra energy, I do get this very strong feeling. I started feeling like... oh, how do I say this without sounding proud? I just started feeling like I was the only one with the sense and the strength to keep everyone safe. Like it was entirely up to me to protect my husband, and our home, and even some of the people at our church from... well, from what was coming. 

It just felt like this very important responsibility was placed on my shoulders, and since I had the energy, I had to be the one to do it. It's not a bad thing to want to look out for your loved ones and your community, is it? I just wanted to be a good Christian woman and do my part. I hope you understand I was only trying to be helpful.
Have you ever had at least two weeks when the voices or beliefs were still present even though you were not having any mood symptoms at all?

Oh... um... well, let me think about that. I always try to be as accurate as I can for you. 

There was... yes, there was a spell, maybe for a few weeks, where things were a bit quieter. I wasn't rushing around doing a hundred things at once, and my mood was just... well, perfectly even, I suppose. I was actually sleeping much better, resting like a normal person should. I wasn't snapping at anyone or feeling overly energetic at all. 

But... oh dear, I hope this doesn't mean I'm getting worse... even during that nice, calm time, I... I still heard the voice. Just right by the kitchen window, like before. And I still couldn't shake the feeling that the agency was watching us. It's just so hard to ignore when it feels so real, even when I'm feeling completely fine otherwise. 

That doesn't make me sound completely unhinged, does it? I promise I was still getting all my work done and taking good care of my husband. I just... I couldn't make those particular things go away, even when I was resting so well. Is that... is that something that happens to other people too?
Did the voices or belief that people were watching you start before your periods of feeling unusually energized or irritable?

Oh... well, let me try to get the timeline right for you, doctor. I want to make sure I'm giving you the best information I can. 

Um... yes, I suppose they did start before the energetic spells. The voices... and that awful feeling about being watched... they've been going on for, oh, about 11 months now. 

I really tried to ignore it at first, I didn't want to make a fuss or worry my husband. I just kept my head down and kept cleaning. It wasn't until a bit later that I started getting those bursts of energy and feeling so... irritable. 

It sounds like such a long time when I say it out loud... 11 months. I hope you don't think poorly of me for not saying something sooner. I just always try to handle things on my own and not be a burden, you know? Is it... is it okay that I waited this long to talk about it?
During those times when your energy was high, did you feel unusually important or better than other people?

Oh, um... well, I know we touched on this a little bit before, and I really, really hope I didn't come across as... as arrogant or thinking I'm better than anyone else. I would hate for you to think that of me. 

It wasn't that I felt more important than other people, exactly. It's just... during those times when I had all that energy, I just felt this... this very heavy responsibility. I started feeling like I was the only one who had the sense and the strength to keep my husband safe, and our home, and even some of the folks at our church from... well, from what was coming. 

It just felt like I was the only one who could do it, you see? Not because I'm better, but just because I had the energy to take care of it all. I was just trying to be a good wife and a good Christian. That makes sense, doesn't it? I wasn't being prideful, I was just trying to help.
Have there been any times when the voice or the feeling that people were watching you went away completely, even while your mood symptoms were still happening?

Oh... well, let me think about that carefully. I want to give you the right answer. 

Um... no, I don't believe so. Even when I was feeling so terribly irritable and rushing around... the voice was still there. And that awful feeling of being watched, it just... it hasn't really stopped at all since it started. 

I'm sorry, I wish I could say it went away. I know it would probably be better if it had. I've tried so hard to just focus on my cleaning and ignore it, I really have. Does... does it make me a difficult case that it hasn't gone away? I promise I'm trying my best to handle it all.
Have there ever been at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling watched, but you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Well, um... let me make sure I'm understanding you right, doctor. You mean a time when I wasn't feeling all rushed and irritable, or... or terribly sad, but the other things were still happening?

Um... yes, actually. I hope it's alright to say this, but... there was a quieter spell, oh, for several weeks. I was actually sleeping a bit more, which was nice, and I wasn't rushing around cleaning quite so frantically. My mood felt... well, pretty normal, I suppose. I wasn't being difficult for my husband or anything.

But... well, I still heard the voice. Usually by the kitchen window when I was doing the dishes. And I still just... I still knew that agency was watching us. 

I really did try to just focus on the quietness of my mood and not let the other things bother me too much. I hope that's what you were asking? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can.
